claims.claim: The modeled 50 um wall law requires ks=3.3464052288e-4 m/s at source pH 5.19608 and sink pH 5.82941, with 0.1-1 uM added NaCl; source/sink target net fluxes are +2.00239e-7/-2.16473e-7 mol m^-2 s^-1.

With a 1.7 mM CO2 / 40 mM bicarbonate pH 7.5 rear solution and CO2-free front, the authors conclude CA stimulates net CO2 flux only when solutions are well buffered. Table II prints unbuffered CA on both sides: 1.1+/-0.9 (n=3); buffered/no CA: 0.7+/-0.5 (n=4); buffered/CA on both sides: 12.7+/-4.3 (n=5), in its printed OCR-damaged units.
claims.interpretation: The unbuffered row is not a matched CA/no-CA comparison, so only the authors explicit buffer-dependence conclusion is used. It blocks transfer of buffered or tracer activity to the low-buffer net wall law; it does not prove every designed surface fails.

claims.claim: hCA IX-c has peak kcat/KM=13.0 uM^-1 s^-1 and Zn-water pKa 6.6 in an 18O equilibrium assay at 25 mM bicarbonate, 25 C and I=0.2 M. A hypothetical 25 nm^2/site full monolayer gives peak-pH ks=8.6348e-4 m/s; an explicitly assumed one-ionization scaling gives source ks=3.2774e-5 m/s and sink ks=1.2521e-4 m/s.
claims.interpretation: None of these are measured immobilized-surface conductances. The assay source concentration is about 266x the modeled source total carbon species and the target source pH is lower than the paper's statement that activity is retained as low as pH 5.5. The pH curve is bell-shaped; the one-ionization figures are sensitivities only. Article has a report inconsistency: Table 1 says 13.0+/-0.1 while text says 13+/-1; computation uses the wider text range.

claims.claim: Fu et al. report up to 2600 GPU, EAD 8.0e11 CA cm^-2 (1.3284e-8 mol m^-2) and 3.7 mM confined CA at pH 7.5 and 37 C; the CO2 separation demo used 20% CO2 feed at 0.48 bar and aqueous Ca(OH)2 sink.
claims.interpretation: 2600 GPU equals 84.88% of target 3063 GPU, but different pH, gas pressure, liquid layer and material. Integrated gas permeance is not the required pair-flux Robin coefficient.

claims.claim: Free BCA increased the initial unbuffered capture rate by 76% at pH 10 but had no positive effect at pH 9 or 11; test used 2 g mineral-water samples, 0.5 mg protein/g, 1.5 bar absolute, 30 C, and mineral-water conductivity 0.472 mS/cm.
claims.interpretation: Does not report area-normalized surface flux, immobilization, target acidity, target gas pressure, or two-direction net flux; no ks can be computed.

claims.claim: At source pCO2 13.8 kPa gauge and dissolved source CO2 about 29.5 mM, the 2026 CO2-driven PDMS-channel study reports 80 nm uncoated PS Gamma_p=-2.9e-10 m^2/s, Dp=5.4e-12 m^2/s and Pe=53.
claims.interpretation: No CA-coated-wall adsorption velocity or wall particle mass closure; the inherited 1.0055e-11 m/s adsorption ceiling is a model target only.

claims.claim: No examined primary report supplies on one material a two-direction measured net-pair-flux ks at target low salt and pH, target humid gas permeance after coating, ion release within budget, and particle adsorption/mass closure below the model ceiling.

A hydrated, tethered His/imidazole proton-relay co-immobilized with CA could reduce interfacial proton-equivalent transfer resistance; this mechanism is already proposed as a surface proton antenna and is not a novelty claim.
